t: Lesson 13 — Step 11: alarms and machine faults
html:
In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 13 is this chapter: it checks that the lesson’s tags are made, that S11_Alarms exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • Inject an overload on Main_Conv: bit 0 latches, the fault lamp flashes, the line stops
  • Inject a jam on Main_Conv: the end-of-line check (LS11) latches bit 2
  • Clear Machine Faults, press Reset, press Start: the alarms clear and the line runs again

Everything so far assumes the machine does what it is told. Real machines do not. A bottle jams; a lens gets dirty and the eye stays dark, or stays made; a motor overload trips and the conveyor stops although the output is still on; a label web breaks; a valve sticks shut. The controller is fine through all of this (the scan goes on, no instruction faults), so nothing tells you unless your program checks. This step is the checks.

The template has three parts for it (chapter 16): LS11, an eye one stop before the end of the line, a red Fault_Lamp and a blue Reset_PB on the console. Each belt also reports Running (the auxiliary contact on its motor contactor, made when the motor really turns), which the template aliases as Main_Conv_Running and Divert_Conv_Running. The alarms are the bits of one DINT, Alarm_Word, shown in Binary:

BitAlarmRaised whenStops the line
0Main conveyor overloadMain_Conveyor commanded, Main_Conv_Running missing for 0.5 syes
1Divert conveyor overloadDivert_Conveyor commanded, Divert_Conv_Running missing for 0.5 syes
2End-of-line checkonce per stop, LS11 disagrees with the tracking for that stop: a bottle missing or one extrayes
3LS1 dark too longthe line running and LS1 dark for 8 syes
4Labeler faultLabel_Fault (step 10) latchedno
5Inlet not fillingSupply_Inlet open with Supply_Low still made for 10 syes
6Case lane drive trippedCase_VFD_Fault (the drive of step 12)no
7Packer infeed fullInfeed_Full: eight bottles waiting to be packedyes
8Camera fault (latched in step 15)a result lost to a full buffer, a missed trigger, or the camera off line for 2 s with the line runningno

Bits 6 and 7 watch the case packer and its drive, which step 12 programs; their alias tags are in your list from chapter 17, so type the rungs now and they will make sense in the next chapter. Add the JSR under step 10 and write:

The rungs

How it fits together

Rungs 0–3, overloads. The output says run; the feedback says not running. Half a second allows for the contactor to pull in. When the timer is done, latch the bit and Alarm_Unack. The one-shot matters: without it an alarm the operator has acknowledged would be raised again every scan while the cause is still there.

Rungs 4–6, the end-of-line check. This is the shift register’s own proof. Once per stop (halfway through the dwell, so the belt is standing still and LS11 has settled, and once only), compare LS11 with what the registers say stands in front of it. LS11 at x 1240 is 27 stops after LS1, so in the dwell frame that is Exist[0].26, Large[0].25, Broken[0].24, and a bottle should be there only if it exists, is large (small ones were diverted), is whole and was not rejected. Expected and dark is EOL_Missing; not expected and made is EOL_Extra. Either is bit 2. A jammed bottle shows up here a few stops after it jams: the bottles behind it pile up, the stops they should be at stay empty, the registers walk on regardless.

Rungs 7–8, LS1 dark too long. The feeder drops a bottle every stop, so LS1 sees one every couple of seconds. Eight seconds dark with the line running means the eye is dirty and stuck off, or nothing is coming. Rung 9 turns the labeler’s fault into bit 4, and rungs 10–11 watch the reservoir: the inlet clears the low float in a second or two, so ten seconds commanded open with the float still made means the valve did not open. Rungs 12–13 are the packer: a drive trip is bit 6, a full infeed bit 7. Rung 14 stops the line on bits 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7, an OTU of Line_Run after step 1’s seal-in, so Start cannot hold while one of them is set.

Rung 15, Reset. One press does two things. It acknowledges (Alarm_Unack off), and it clears every alarm whose cause has gone. An end-of-line alarm is different: its cause is that the registers no longer describe the belt, so Reset clears the register words and sets EOL_Inhibit, and the check stays off until the first bottle tracked since the reset reaches LS11 (rung 6). That is how a real line recovers after a jam: clear the jam, reset the tracking, purge the line. Rung 16 lets a drive trip clear itself from the alarm word once the drive reports healthy. Rungs 17–18, the lamp: it flashes while an alarm is unacknowledged and is steady while an acknowledged alarm is still set. Off means healthy.

A machine fault is not a controller fault

Chapter 9’s major fault is the controller stopping itself: an instruction it cannot execute. The scan stops and Communications → Clear Faults clears it. A machine fault is everything in this chapter: the controller is healthy, the scan runs, and the only way anyone finds out is a rung like these. The first kind is the PLC protecting itself; the second is your program protecting the machine, the product and the people near it.

Inject a fault

The simulator can break the machine on purpose. Tools → Inject Machine Fault… lists, for the parts on your floor, a bottle jammed on a conveyor, a sensor with a dirty lens stuck on or stuck off, a conveyor overload, a labeler web break, a reservoir inlet stuck shut, a drive trip, and more. Each is logged and drawn with a red dashed outline. Tools → Clear Machine Faults or Reset Sim takes them away; click a jammed bottle in Run mode to free it. Tools → Fault Drill… injects a random one as a timed exercise, which is how you practise finding a fault you did not choose.

Run it

Start the line and leave it three minutes: Alarm_Word stays 0 and the lamp stays dark. Press Stop and Start at any moment you like, mid-step, mid-dwell, mid-fill: still 0. Now break things, one at a time, with Clear Machine Faults, Reset and Start between each. Overload on Main_Conv: at the next step bit 0 latches, the line stops, the lamp flashes. Jam on Main_Conv: a few stops later LS11 disagrees with the registers, bit 2; free the bottle, Reset (the registers clear and the check waits), Start. Dirty LS1, stuck off: eight seconds later, bit 3; after the reset, bit 2 follows, because the bottles that passed LS1 while it was blind were never entered in the registers. Labeler web break: bit 4 at once, the line keeps running. Inlet stuck shut: nothing until the reservoir falls to the low float; ten seconds after that, bit 5.

Try it

Add an alarm for the head tank (Tank_Low): step 6 already stops the line on it, but nothing tells the operator why. Give it a free bit, latch it like the others, and make Reset clear it once the tank has recovered. Then run the fault drill for ten minutes and keep a log of what you found and how long each took.

rungs.head: S11_Alarms · Rung 0
rungs.comment: MAIN CONVEYOR OVERLOAD: Fwd is commanded but the running feedback from the motor contactor is missing for half a second

pred.q: Line_Run is on, Main_Conveyor is on and Main_Conv_Running is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Main_OL_T times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, Main_Conveyor (LogixPro O:2/0 · Main conveyor motor) is on and Main_Conv_Running (Main conveyor running feedback (motor contactor)) is off, the rung runs the timer Main_OL_T (Main conveyor overload timer (no running feedback)) toward 500 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIC(Main_Conveyor) Examine If Closed asks: true when Main_Conveyor is on.
  3. XIO(Main_Conv_Running) Examine If Open asks: true when Main_Conv_Running is off.
  4. TON(Main_OL_T,500,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Main_OL_T toward 500 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Main_OL_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: S11_Alarms · Rung 1
rungs.comment: Latch alarm bit 0 and mark it unacknowledged. The one-shot means an acknowledged alarm is not re-raised every scan while the cause is still there
rungs.words: When Main_OL_T.DN (the done bit of Main_OL_T: Main conveyor overload timer (no running feedback)) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Alarm_Word.0 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full) on and latches Alarm_Unack (New alarm, not yet acknowledged (Reset)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Main_OL_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Main_OL_T.DN is on.
  2. ONS(OL_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in OL_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Alarm_Word.0) Output Latch does: latches Alarm_Word.0 on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Alarm_Unack) Output Latch does: latches Alarm_Unack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Alarm_Word.0 stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: S11_Alarms · Rung 4
rungs.comment: END-OF-LINE CHECK: once per stop, halfway through the dwell, compare LS11 at 1240 with what the registers say stands there. Only large, whole, passed bottles reach the end, so the registers expect one when Exist 26, Large 25, not Broken 24 and not Reject 13 (the dwell frame, chapter 10; a rejected bottle went to the shredder at the scrap gate). A bottle expected but missing is a jam or a lost bottle upstream; a bottle there but not expected means the tracking is out of step
rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, EOL_Inhibit (Tracking cleared by Reset: the end-of-line check waits until the first bottle tracked since then reaches LS11) is off, Dwell.TT (the timing bit of Dwell: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle) is on, Dwell.ACC (the accumulated value of Dwell: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle) is at least 500 and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if Exist[0].26 (Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher) is on, Large[0].25 (Large bottle (LogixPro B3:20). During the dwell: filler 5, capper 8, scrap gate 12, divert gate 19; after the shift one bit higher) is on, Broken[0].24 (Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher) is off, Reject[0].13 (Bad bottle (the camera found no cap, no label or a short fill), one bit per stop from the stop past the camera. During the dwell: scrap gate 0, divert gate 7; after the shift one bit higher) is off and LS11 (End-of-line eye at 1240: verifies the tracking (only large, whole bottles reach it)) is off, it latches EOL_Missing (LS11 dark when the registers said a large, whole bottle was there) on; if either (Exist[0].26 is off), (Large[0].25 is off), (Broken[0].24 is on) or (Reject[0].13 is on) and LS11 is on, it latches EOL_Extra (LS11 saw a bottle the registers did not expect) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIO(EOL_Inhibit) Examine If Open asks: true when EOL_Inhibit is off.
  3. XIC(Dwell.TT) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.TT is on.
  4. GEQ(Dwell.ACC,500) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Dwell.ACC is at least 500.
  5. ONS(EOL_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in EOL_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  6. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Exist[0].26) Examine If Closed asks: true when Exist[0].26 is on.
    2. XIC(Large[0].25) Examine If Closed asks: true when Large[0].25 is on.
    3. XIO(Broken[0].24) Examine If Open asks: true when Broken[0].24 is off.
    4. XIO(Reject[0].13) Examine If Open asks: true when Reject[0].13 is off.
    5. XIO(LS11) Examine If Open asks: true when LS11 is off.
    6. OTL(EOL_Missing) Output Latch does: latches EOL_Missing on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
      Path 1
      1. XIO(Exist[0].26) Examine If Open asks: true when Exist[0].26 is off.
      Path 2
      1. XIO(Large[0].25) Examine If Open asks: true when Large[0].25 is off.
      Path 3
      1. XIC(Broken[0].24) Examine If Closed asks: true when Broken[0].24 is on.
      Path 4
      1. XIC(Reject[0].13) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reject[0].13 is on.
    2. XIC(LS11) Examine If Closed asks: true when LS11 is on.
    3. OTL(EOL_Extra) Output Latch does: latches EOL_Extra on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: EOL_Missing stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

pred.q: EOL_Inhibit is on and Exist[0].26 is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: EOL_Inhibit is unlatched.

rungs.words: When EOL_Inhibit (Tracking cleared by Reset: the end-of-line check waits until the first bottle tracked since then reaches LS11) is on and Exist[0].26 (Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher) is on, the rung unlatches EOL_Inhibit.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(EOL_Inhibit) Examine If Closed asks: true when EOL_Inhibit is on.

  3. OTU(EOL_Inhibit) Output Unlatch does: unlatches EOL_Inhibit. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears EOL_Inhibit when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S11_Alarms · Rung 15
rungs.comment: RESET: acknowledge everything, and clear each alarm whose detecting timer is no longer done. With the line stopped most timers have reset, so Reset is a reset attempt: if the cause is still there, the alarm comes back after its delay. An end-of-line alarm means the registers no longer describe the belt, so Reset also clears them: bottles already on the belt run out unprocessed and the check waits for the first bottle tracked from the head
rungs.words: When Reset_PB (Blue Reset button: acknowledge alarms and clear the ones whose cause is gone) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: it unlatches Alarm_Unack (New alarm, not yet acknowledged (Reset)); if Main_OL_T.DN (the done bit of Main_OL_T: Main conveyor overload timer (no running feedback)) is off, it unlatches Alarm_Word.0 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full); if Div_OL_T.DN (the done bit of Div_OL_T: Divert conveyor overload timer (no running feedback)) is off, it unlatches Alarm_Word.1 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full); if Alarm_Word.2 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full) is on, it clears Exist[0] (Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher) to 0, clears Exist[1] (Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher) to 0, clears Large[0] (Large bottle (LogixPro B3:20). During the dwell: filler 5, capper 8, scrap gate 12, divert gate 19; after the shift one bit higher) to 0, clears Large[1] (Large bottle (LogixPro B3:20). During the dwell: filler 5, capper 8, scrap gate 12, divert gate 19; after the shift one bit higher) to 0, clears Broken[0] (Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher) to 0, clears Broken[1] (Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher) to 0, clears Reject[0] (Bad bottle (the camera found no cap, no label or a short fill), one bit per stop from the stop past the camera. During the dwell: scrap gate 0, divert gate 7; after the shift one bit higher) to 0, clears Reject[1] (Bad bottle (the camera found no cap, no label or a short fill), one bit per stop from the stop past the camera. During the dwell: scrap gate 0, divert gate 7; after the shift one bit higher) to 0, latches EOL_Inhibit (Tracking cleared by Reset: the end-of-line check waits until the first bottle tracked since then reaches LS11) on, unlatches EOL_Missing (LS11 dark when the registers said a large, whole bottle was there), unlatches EOL_Extra (LS11 saw a bottle the registers did not expect) and unlatches Alarm_Word.2; if LS1_Dark_T.DN (the done bit of LS1_Dark_T: LS1 dark too long timer) is off, it unlatches Alarm_Word.3 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full); if Label_Fault (Latched on the labeler Error input (end of roll or a missed label); Enter clears it) is off, it unlatches Alarm_Word.4 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full); if Inlet_T.DN (the done bit of Inlet_T: Inlet not filling timer) is off, it unlatches Alarm_Word.5 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full);
